title: Defect-engineered N-doped carbon stabilizes Cu+ active sites for bifunctional CO2 electroreduction to CO and formate
content:
RSC Adv., 2026, 16,4535-4548
DOI: 10.1039/D5RA08966B, Paper
Open Access
  This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 3.0 Unported Licence.
Pirapath Arkasalerks, Phongphot Sakulaue, Pongkarn Chakthranont, Kanokwan Kongpatpanich, Khanin Nueangnoraj
Defect-engineered N-doped carbon from tea leaves stabilizes Cu+ via Cu–Nx sites, enabling durable bifunctional CO2 electroreduction to CO and formate. A robust Cu+/Cu0 interface suppresses H2 evolution and boosts selectivity and stability.
